drafts.walkScript: Start with fish and swim. Swim is how a fish moves. Fly is how a bird moves. A bird can sing, but that is a sound, not how it moves. Float is not how a bird gets about.
Start with pen and write. A pen is used to write. A knife is used to cut. Draw is another job for a pen. A knife can spread butter, but its main job is to cut.
Start with whisper and quiet. A whisper is quiet. A shout is loud. Soft is like quiet, which suits a whisper. Angry is a feeling, not how a shout sounds.
Start with chapter and novel. A chapter is one part of a novel. A scene is one part of a play. A line is part of a scene, which turns the pair round. A ticket is only for watching a play.

Start with breeze and gale. A breeze is light wind and a gale is strong wind. A shower is light rain and a downpour is heavy rain. Drizzle is lighter than a shower, the other way round. A kite goes with wind, not rain.
Start with novel and chapter. A chapter is one part of a novel. A verse is one part of a poem. A book is bigger than a poem, which turns the pair round. An author writes a poem but is not part of it.

Start with dictionary and word. A dictionary is a book full of words. An atlas is a book full of maps. A library holds atlases, which turns the pair round. Geography is the subject, not what fills the book.

Start with sketch and painting. A sketch is a rough first try at a painting. A draft is a rough first try at an essay. An outline comes before a draft, which turns the pair round. A pen is only the tool.

Start with apprentice and master. An apprentice is a learner who grows into a master. A sapling is a young tree that grows into an oak. An acorn comes before a sapling, the other way round. A branch is only part of a tree.
